_note: Draft copy. Edit wording to match your recording protocol. 'final_keys' are the labels YOU assign in the web app; contributors only pick one 'key' (a coarser, easier-to-tell-apart card). Category key 'silicone_mask' intentionally maps to final key 'silicon_mask'. Summaries: 12 words max. 'confused_with' pairs are symmetrical.

categories.name: Live person
categories.summary: Just you, live, in front of the camera.
steps: Hold the phone at arm's length with your face in the oval.
Look at the camera and blink naturally.
Stay in frame for the whole recording.
dos: Glasses on or off is fine

categories.name: Printed photo
categories.summary: A flat printed photo of a face, held up to the camera.
needs: A printed photo of a face (paper)
steps: Hold the printout in front of the camera.
Fill the oval with the face in the photo.
Tilt it slightly and keep it steady.
donts: Don't show a photo on a screen (that's a different card)

categories.name: Photo cut-out mask
categories.summary: A printed face cut out and worn like a mask.
steps: Cut out the printed face. Eye holes are optional.
Wear or hold it over your face.
Look at the camera and move slightly.
dos: Make the cut-out cover your whole face
donts: Don't just hold a flat photo (that's Printed photo)

categories.name: Curved printed photo
categories.summary: A printed face photo bent around a bottle, cylinder or head-shaped object.
needs: A bottle, cylinder or similar object
steps: Wrap the photo around the object.
Hold it up so the face looks toward the camera.
Turn it slowly left and right.
dos: Keep the face visible and centered

categories.name: Phone screen
categories.summary: A video or photo of a face shown on a phone screen.
needs: A video or photo of a face
steps: Play the face video on the second phone at full brightness.
Hold it in front of the camera so the face fills the oval.
Keep both phones steady.
donts: Don't cover the screen with your hand

categories.name: Computer screen
categories.summary: A face shown on a laptop or desktop monitor.
needs: A video or photo of a face
steps: Show the face full-screen on the computer.
Point the camera at the screen from about arm's length.
Avoid glare and keep steady.
dos: Fill the oval with the face on screen
donts: Don't show yourself live on the screen

categories.name: 3D cardboard mask
categories.summary: A 3D face mask built from connected cardboard pieces.
steps: Assemble the pieces into a face-shaped 3D mask.
Wear it or hold it in front of your face.
Look at the camera and turn slightly.
dos: Make sure the face is recognisable
donts: Don't use a single flat piece (that's Photo cut-out mask)

categories.name: Latex mask
categories.summary: A stretchy rubber mask shaped like a face.
steps: Put the mask on.
Look at the camera and move your head slightly.
Keep the mask in place for the whole recording.
donts: Don't use a mask that only covers the eyes

categories.name: Silicone mask
steps: Put the mask on.
Look at the camera and move your head slightly.
Keep the mask in place for the whole recording.
donts: Don't use a rubber party mask (that's Latex mask)
